about: Outbound marketing rules for six EMEA markets. Built from public sources. Not legal advice. Each market records how its rules were verified and when.

bases.opt_out: Allowed without consent. Identify yourself, offer an opt out and honour objections.
bases.consent: Needs prior consent unless an exception applies.
bases.presumed_consent: Needs a concrete, documented reason to expect the recipient wants the contact.

UK.name: United Kingdom
UK.existing_customer: Soft opt in for individual subscribers: details collected in a sale or negotiation, similar products, a chance to opt out at collection and in every message.

email_company.summary: Companies are corporate subscribers. The PECR email rule does not apply to them, so no consent is needed. Name the sender, give a valid opt out address and honour opt outs.

email_sole_trader.summary: Sole traders and some partnerships are individual subscribers. Email needs consent or the soft opt in.

call_company.summary: Live calls are allowed unless the company has objected. Screen against both the TPS and the CTPS, because some businesses register on each.

call_sole_trader.summary: Live calls are allowed unless the number is on the TPS or CTPS or the person has objected.

verification.notes: ICO business to business marketing guidance. Email to corporate subscribers needs no consent under PECR. Sole traders need consent or the soft opt in. Live B2B calls must be screened against both the TPS and the CTPS.

IE.name: Ireland
IE.law: European Communities (Electronic Communications Networks and Services) (Privacy and Electronic Communications) Regulations 2011, S.I. No. 336 of 2011, Regulation 13
IE.existing_customer: Regulation 13(11): details collected in a sale, similar products, a chance to object at collection and in every message, contact within 12 months of the sale.

email_company.summary: Regulation 13(4): email to a subscriber that is not a natural person is allowed unless it has objected.

email_sole_trader.summary: Regulation 13(2): email to an address used mainly for their business, about that business only, falls outside the consent rule in 13(1). Honour objections.

call_company.summary: Regulation 13(5): calls are allowed unless the subscriber has objected or opted out in the National Directory Database. Regulation 13(6): calls to a mobile need consent.

call_sole_trader.summary: Regulation 13(5): landline calls are allowed unless the person has objected or opted out in the National Directory Database. Regulation 13(6): calls to a mobile need consent.

verification.notes: S.I. 336/2011 Regulation 13. 13(1): consent for email to natural persons. 13(2): carves out email to a business address about that business. 13(4): companies are opt out. 13(5): calls are screened against objections and the National Directory Database. 13(6): mobile calls need consent for every subscriber, companies included. 13(11): customer exception with a 12 month limit.

DE.name: Germany
DE.regulator: No single regulator. Competitors and consumer associations enforce through the courts. Bundesnetzagentur acts on calls to consumers.
DE.existing_customer: §7(3): address received from a customer in a sale, own similar products, no objection, a clear opt out at collection and in every message.

email_company.summary: §7(2) no. 2: advertising by email needs prior express consent. This applies to B2B email too.

email_sole_trader.summary: §7(2) no. 2: advertising by email needs prior express consent, including to sole traders.

call_company.summary: §7(2) no. 1: calls to other market participants need at least presumed consent. A concrete business reason must exist before the call.

call_sole_trader.summary: §7(2) no. 1: sole traders called in their business capacity are other market participants. Presumed consent applies.

verification.notes: UWG §7(2) no. 1 for calls: express consent for consumers, at least presumed consent for other market participants. §7(2) no. 2 for email: prior express consent for every recipient. §7(3) for the customer exception. Text read on buzer.de because the official site could not be reached.

FR.name: France
FR.law: Code des postes et des communications électroniques (CPCE) article L.34-5
FR.regulator: Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL)
FR.existing_customer: L.34-5: details collected in a sale, analogous products, a chance to object at collection and in every message.

email_company.summary: CNIL guidance: email to professionals is allowed without consent if the subject relates to their job and they can object.

email_sole_trader.summary: The statute requires consent for individuals. CNIL guidance treats professional addresses as opt out when the subject relates to their job. Confirm this for sole traders.

call_company.summary: Live calls to professionals are allowed. Honour objections.

call_sole_trader.summary: Calls about their trade are allowed. From 11 August 2026 calls to consumers need prior consent and Bloctel has closed. Confirm a sole trader is called as a professional, not as a consumer.

verification.notes: CNIL guidance not confirmed. The Légifrance and CNIL pages could not be loaded, so the opt out rule for professionals still rests on unchecked guidance.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.existing_customer: Article 11.7(4): details collected from customers in a sale, own similar products, a chance to object at collection and in every message. The three year window for calling customers is not in the statute text. Check ACM guidance.

email_company.summary: Article 11.7(1): email marketing needs prior consent from the end user, companies included. Article 11.7(3): no consent is needed for contact details the company published for this purpose.

email_sole_trader.summary: Article 11.7(1): email marketing needs prior consent. Article 11.7(3): no consent is needed for contact details the sole trader published for this purpose.

call_company.summary: Article 11.7(2) covers calls to natural persons only. Live calls to companies are allowed. Honour objections.

call_sole_trader.summary: Article 11.7(2): calls to natural persons need consent. Article 11.7(3): no consent is needed for a number the sole trader published for this purpose. The Bel me niet register has closed.

verification.notes: Telecommunicatiewet article 11.7. 11.7(1): consent for email, companies included. 11.7(2): consent for calls to natural persons. 11.7(3): exception for contact details published for this purpose. 11.7(4): customer exception. The three year window for calling customers was not found in the statute text.

ES.name: Spain
ES.law: Ley 34/2002 (LSSI) article 21 and Ley 11/2022 General de Telecomunicaciones (LGTel) article 66
ES.regulator: Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD)
ES.existing_customer: LSSI article 21.2: prior contract, data obtained lawfully, own similar products, a simple free way to object at collection and in every message.

email_company.summary: LSSI article 21.1: commercial email needs a prior request or express consent. This applies to companies too.

email_sole_trader.summary: LSSI article 21.1: commercial email needs a prior request or express consent.

call_company.summary: LGTel article 66.1(b): calls are allowed with consent or another GDPR article 6.1 basis, such as legitimate interest. Screen against Lista Robinson and honour objections.

call_sole_trader.summary: LGTel article 66.1(b): calls are allowed with consent or another GDPR article 6.1 basis, such as legitimate interest. Screen against Lista Robinson and honour objections.

verification.notes: LSSI article 21.1: consent for email. 21.2: customer exception. LGTel article 66.1(b): calls may rest on another GDPR article 6.1 basis. Lista Robinson screening comes from data protection law and AEPD guidance, not these two articles, and was not checked.
